{{nihongo|'''Amawake Toyohime Shrine'''|天別豊姫神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Bingo Province]].

[[File:Amawaketoyohime-jinja, torii.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Torii}}]]
'''Amawake Toyohime Shrine''' (あまわけとよひめじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Kannabe-chō Kawakita, {{ill|Fukuyama, Hiroshima|Q661038|qid=Q661038}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|Q617375|qid=Q617375}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking}} it was classified as a {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}}.

In ancient times it was also known as “Kannabe Daimyōjin” and “Kannobi Daimyōjin.” The shrine is situated on the mid-slope of Mt. Kōyō to the south of the townscape of Kannabe, and it is said that the place name “Kannabe” derives from this shrine.

=== Enshrined deities ===
Five deities are enshrined.
; Principal deities
:* {{ill|Toyotama-hime|lt=Toyotama-hime|Q2329261|qid=Q2329261|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime no Mikoto}} (とよたまひめのみこと) – regarded as the original enshrined deity.
:* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Hayasusanoo no Mikoto}} (はやすさのおのみこと)
:* {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi no Kami}} (ことしろぬしのかみ)
; Associated deities
:* {{ill|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|Q65318|qid=Q65318}} (きびつひこのみこと)
:* {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|Q1640658|qid=Q1640658|lt=Hi no Kagutsuchi no Kami}} (ひのかぐつちのかみ)

The two associated deities were enshrined together in Taishō 3 (1914), when Kibitsu Shrine in the Kake area of Kawakita Village was merged into this shrine.

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
In ancient times, the area around the shrine is said to have been an inlet of the sea called “Anaumi.” According to shrine tradition, it was originally enshrined as Iso Shrine on a rocky shore in Amitsukidani, and later relocated further inland to Mount Konakayama<ref>“Place Names of Hiroshima Prefecture,” entry on Amawake Toyohime Shrine.</ref>. Within the same {{ill|Bingo Province|Q1049113|qid=Q1049113}}, there are {{ill|Nunakuma Shrine|Q11554446|qid=Q11554446}} (in Tomo-chō, Fukuyama City), which enshrines Toyotama-hime’s father Toyotamahiko ({{ill|Watatsumi|Q1474187|qid=Q1474187|lt=Ōwatatsumi no Mikoto}}), and Sorahiko Shrine in {{ill|Shōbara|Q857234|qid=Q857234}}, which enshrines her husband Sorahiko ({{ill|Hoori|Q1051960|qid=Q1051960|lt=Hikohohodemi no Mikoto}}); this shrine lies between them.

In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=national histories}}, it is recorded that in Genkei 2 ({{ill|878|Q23910|qid=Q23910}}) the shrine deity “Amawake Toyohime no Kami” was promoted in {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade.

In the Jinmyōchō of the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} compiled in Enchō 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it is listed as “Amawake Toyohime Shrine” in {{ill|Yasuna district|Q10947253|qid=Q10947253}} of Bingo Province, and is classified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

During the Kenmu era ({{ill|1334|Q6007|qid=Q6007}}–{{ill|1338|Q6044|qid=Q6044}}), when Asayama Kagetsura built {{ill|Kannabe Castle|Q11590904|qid=Q11590904}} on Mt. Kōyō, the shrine was made the castle’s guardian deity and relocated to its present site on the mid-slope of Mt. Kōyō.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was venerated by the lords of the {{ill|Fukuyama Domain|Q909278|qid=Q909278|lt=Fukuyama Domain}}, namely the {{ill|Mizuno clan|Q2975321|qid=Q2975321}} and the {{ill|Abe clan|Q11657874|qid=Q11657874|lt=Abe clan}}.

In Meiji 1 ({{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}}), an investigation by the Fukuyama Domain identified it as a Shikinaisha, and in Meiji 2 ({{ill|1869|Q7720|qid=Q7720}}) its official name was set as “Amawake Toyohime Shrine.” In Meiji 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}) it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, and in Shōwa 15 ({{ill|1940|Q18633|qid=Q18633}}) it was elevated to a {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}}.

=== Divine ranks ===
* Genkei 2 ({{ill|878|Q23910|qid=Q23910}}), 11th month, 13th day: promotion from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}) – recorded as “Amawake Toyohime no Kami.”

=== Shrine grounds ===
[[File:Amawaketoyohime-jinja, honden.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Main hall}}]]
The main hall was constructed in Meiji 11 ({{ill|1878|Q7776|qid=Q7776}}) and is a three-bay shrine in the {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}} style.

=== Auxiliary shrines ===
* Tenno Shrine
* Inari Shrine
* Kō Shrine
* Benzaiten Shrine
* Tenjin Shrine
In addition, many other small shrines stand within the precincts.
